A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Glove2Hand and contain readable main texts, Appendices A-D, equations, tables, and figures. Corresponding content can be matched reliably, including material shifted within the appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation experiments, component ablations, contact-estimation and hand-tracking results, and a human evaluation in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1-4, the human-rating distributions, and Appendix Table 7.

M1.justification: The Gaussian hand model, diffusion restorer, objectives, and inference pipeline remain unchanged. Appendix B newly documents pose-retargeting calibration as a data-collection detail; it does not establish that the implemented method changed between versions.

E1.justification: Both versions use HandSense and HOT3D and retain the same interaction tasks, subjects, objects, downstream applications, and in-domain, cross-subject, and in-the-wild evaluation scenarios. The added calibration poses do not constitute a new evaluated task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Table 1 and Figures 6 and 15. Tables 3 and 4 retain the same PressureVision++, UmeTrack, and training-data comparisons.

E3.justification: No previously stated split, metric, training budget, model configuration, or evaluation procedure is revised. The added calibration description discloses data preparation without establishing that existing experimental settings were changed.

E4.justification: Table 2 and Figure 8 retain identical component ablations, and the generalization examples and supplementary qualitative comparisons are unchanged. No calibration ablation, robustness test, or additional case study is reported.

E5.justification: Human-rating distributions, response counts, and mean-opinion-score reporting are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1-4 and 7 and the qualitative result figures are identical. For example, Glove2Hand retains FID 30.1, FVD 19.5, and FVD-long 24.5 in Table 1. The calibration paragraph supplies no new experimental results.

T1.justification: Section 3's problem formulation and Gaussian deformation and relighting mathematics are unchanged. The new calibration paragraph contains no formal optimization objective, derivation, proposition, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about glove-to-hand synthesis, HandSense's synchronized sensor signals, and benefits for contact estimation and occluded hand tracking.

C2.justification: Appendix B adds a specific explanation of how glove thickness disrupts pose transfer: an OK-sign glove pose can produce separated bare-hand fingertips. It explains joint-displacement calibration as the remedy, extending v1's discussion of glove-size mismatch and rendering artifacts.

D1.justification: v2 newly describes collecting standard poses such as pinch and OK signs from each participant, optimizing per-joint displacements, and applying them to recorded glove poses. This adds useful calibration information, although the optimization objective and fitting parameters remain unspecified.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and novelty positioning are unchanged. Updated reference back-links reflect appendix pagination; the new generic analogy to robotic motion retargeting does not substantively reposition the work.

P1.justification: v2 adds one titled explanatory paragraph, 'Motion Retarget from Gloves to Bare Hands,' in Appendix B. The main text and section sequence remain unchanged; other textual edits concern the arXiv version stamp and reference back-links.

P2.justification: The appendix reflows: Section D starts on page 14 instead of page 13, training details continue onto page 15, and Figure 12 and Table 7 move upward within that page. Figures 13-14 also shift slightly. No figure or table is added, removed, or substantively redesigned.

improvement.justification: Appendix B fills a practical documentation gap by explaining contact errors caused by glove thickness and describing the calibration used to address them. This modestly improves understanding and reproducibility. The optimization remains incompletely specified, and the unchanged experiments provide no additional validation of calibration's effect.
